newsitem.title: HONG KONG: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.
newsitem.headline: Hong Kong gold ends down on overseas sales.

text.p: Hong Kong gold slid lower on Monday on brisk overseas sales with little physical demand to counter the drop, bullion traders said.
Much of the sales originated from professionals and when London opened the Hong Kong market dropped even further on sales triggered by heavily bearish sentiment, they said.
A number of factors contributed to bearishness in the British colony, bullion traders said.
Physical demand was largely satisfied around the US$378 per ounce level, Japanese traders bought gold earlier when the dollar/yen was lower and producers were still eager to hedge, they said.
Having broken the $375 per ounce level, gold could test as low as $372-373 per ounce, bullion dealers said.
Bullion ended at $374.90/375.40 an ounce on Monday against Hong Kong's Saturday close at $376.30/80 and New York's $376.10/60 close on Friday.
Local gold ended HK$9 lower at HK$3,463 a tael.
The carryover charge at the Chinese Gold and Silver Exchange Society remained unchanged from its previous fix at 0.
